[[Avispa Fukuoka|Avispa]] vs [[RB Omiya Ardija|Ardija]] | average attendance = 15,797 | prevseason = [[2010 J.League Division 1|2010]] | nextseason = [[2012 J.League Division 1|2012]] }} The '''2011 J.League Division 1 season''' was the 46th season of professional [[association football|football]] in [[Football in Japan|Japan]], and the 19th since the establishment of the [[J.League]]. The season began on March 5 and concluded on December 3. The season was put on hold from March 12 to April 23 due to the aftermath of the [[2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami]],{{cite web|title=J.League agrees to resume games on April 23 |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/soccer/03/22/jleague.resume/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104033721/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/soccer/03/22/jleague.resume/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 4, 2012|work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=27 March 2011}} therefore canceling a planned five-week summer break between June 27–July 29 in order to allow preparation of the [[Japan national football team|Japan national team]] for the [[2011 Copa América]].{{cite web|url=http://www.j-league.or.jp/release/000/00003808.html |title=2011 J.League tournament details |publisher=J.League official website |language=ja |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101224083119/http://www.j-league.or.jp/release/000/00003808.html |archive-date=2010-12-24 }} The 2011 J.League Division 1 champion also qualified to the [[2011 FIFA Club World Cup]] as the host team, entering the qualifying play-off round. [[Kashiwa Reysol]] won a second [[List of Japanese football champions|league title]], their first in 39 years and first in the professional J.League era. They also became the first champions to win the title the season after being promoted as [[List of winners of J.League Division 2 and predecessors|second division champions]]. ==Clubs== [[FC Tokyo]], [[Kyoto Sanga FC|Kyoto Sanga]] and [[Shonan Bellmare]] were relegated at the end of the [[2010 J.League Division 1|2010 season]] after finishing in the bottom three places of the table. Shonan had only played one season in Division 1 while Kyoto had enjoyed a three-year stay. FC Tokyo had been in the top flight for eleven seasons. The three relegated teams were replaced by [[2010 J.League Division 2]] champions [[Kashiwa Reysol]], runners-up [[Ventforet Kofu]] and third-placed team [[Avispa Fukuoka]]. League Division 1] |notes=† Team played previous season in J2.|date=August 2013}} ;Notes *Note 1: Kashima Antlers played one game at the [[Japan National Stadium]] in Tokyo as the [[Kashima Soccer Stadium]] in [[Kashima, Ibaraki|Kashima]] was damaged in the [[2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami]]. ==In popular culture== This particular season was used as reference in the movie ''[[Detective Conan: The Eleventh Striker]]''. Many players in real life actually provide cameo roles for the film, including [[Kazuyoshi Miura]] ([[Yokohama FC]]), [[Yasuhito Endō]] ([[Gamba Osaka]]), [[Yasuyuki Konno]] (Gamba Osaka), [[Kengo Nakamura]] ([[Kawasaki Frontale]]), and [[Seigo Narazaki]] ([[Nagoya Grampus]]). In the movie, a bomber threatens to bomb all the stadiums unless certain conditions are met. The main character, [[Jimmy Kudo|Conan Edogawa]], must solve the case and find the culprit. In the movie, two additional fictional teams are added to the squad: Tokyo Spirits and Big Osaka, making the league with 20 teams. ==References== {{Japanese Club Football|group=first}} {{2011 in Japanese football}} {{2011 in Asian Football (AFC)}} {{J1 League champions}} {{DEFAULTSORT:J.League Division 1}} [[Category:2011 J.League|1]] [[Category:J1 League seasons|2011]] [[Category:2011 in Asian men's top-tier association football leagues|Japan]]
